What this evaluates

Which model knows Medicare's rules well enough to triage a denied skilled-nursing claim? 300 synthetic Medicare fee-for-service Part A claims with raw 835 remittance codes and the facility's records, and no payer manual: the rules (42 CFR, the CMS manuals, the X12 code list) are in RULES.md and the model must know them. 110 ordinary items; 190 where the rule changes the answer: filing limits from the Through date, the redetermination deadline (125 days after the remittance), new benefit periods, days past day 100, and a three-day stay counted from the admission order.

A pass of triage-check means: Root cause, correctability, next action and deadline match the key computed from RULES.md; the deadline must be the last day the rules allow.

directional

Recommend gpt-5.6-sol · lowest cost

$0.0166 per success · required check 276/300 passed

Of the 3 candidates that pass every gate, gpt-5.6-sol has the lowest generation cost per success ($0.0166). It beats the control sonnet-5.

No pairwise comparison was available this run.

The spec declares no minimum meaningful difference, gpt-5.6-sol: required-check-pass-rate 276/300 has a 95% interval down to 0.884, below the gate 0.9, gpt-5.6-sol: reliability 276/300 has a 95% interval down to 0.884, below the gate 0.9, so this result is directional only.
